Hypothesis: Building on the original idea, we propose that radiotherapy-induced, transient TGF‐β1 increases in patients with solid tumors can prime a specific subset of CD8⁺ T cells into a reversible pre‐exhausted state. This state, if properly characterized using advanced single-cell transcriptomics and real-time cytokine monitoring, represents an optimal period for immunotherapeutic intervention. By integrating nanoparticle-mediated chemo-immunotherapy to further boost CD8⁺ T cell infiltration and by employing machine learning algorithms to accurately predict the timing of this transient window, we anticipate that PD‐1 inhibitors administered at this precise juncture will most effectively reactivate the primed T cells. This strategy not only retains the core mechanistic framework of the original hypothesis but also addresses previous concerns regarding immune cell count variability and mechanistic clarity by incorporating additional biomarkers and technological tools.
Abstract: We hypothesize that radiotherapy in solid tumors induces a transient systemic surge in TGF‐β1 that, especially when combined with nanoparticle‐mediated chemo-immunotherapy, primes a distinct subset of CD8⁺ T cells into a reversible “pre‐exhausted” state. This transient state can be precisely detected using a combination of advanced single-cell transcriptomic profiling, real-time multiplex cytokine assays (including high-sensitivity TGF‐β1 measurements), and machine learning algorithms designed to define the optimal temporal window. Timely administration of PD‐1 inhibitors during this window is predicted to reinvigorate these primed T cells, overcoming TGF‐β1–mediated immunosuppression and thereby enhancing anti-tumor immunity and clinical outcomes. This multi-modal approach leverages contemporary technological advances to integrate radiotherapy-induced cytokine dynamics with additional immune-modulatory strategies for precision cancer immunotherapy.
Orignal_vs_New: The revised hypothesis retains the original core concept that radiotherapy induces a transient TGF‐β1 surge which primes a subset of CD8⁺ T cells into a reversible pre‐exhausted state detectable by advanced modalities. It expands on this framework by incorporating nanoparticle-mediated chemo-immunotherapy to enhance CD8⁺ T cell infiltration and by employing real-time multiplex cytokine monitoring and machine learning algorithms for precise determination of the optimal PD‐1 inhibitor administration window. These additions directly address the review's concerns regarding the broad reduction in immune cells, the need for additional mechanistic clarity, and the importance of robust, data-driven temporal mapping, thereby enhancing both the innovative scope and practical implementability of the hypothesis.
